confirmed_scope: Random world spawners and bounded spawn areas
recovery_policy: Recover original definitions, Blueprint relationships, placement and rules before replacing them. Preserve existing identifiers and authored content. Distinguish reconstruction choices from recovered behavior.
semantics_to_recover: Whether quest groups represent selection pools, linked quest chains, encounter groups or another authored structure; do not equate them with player parties
What each spawner produces: AI, encounters, quest givers, objectives, pickups or another class
Spawn area shape, location membership, eligibility, activation, cooldown and population rules
Quest selection weights, exclusions, prerequisites, repeatability and regeneration/reset rules
Whether reward rolls happen at generation, acceptance, completion or another original event
Reward pools, weights, quantity ranges, player/group entitlements and difficulty/level scaling
multiplayer_implementation_requirements: The server owns spawn decisions, random quest selection, reward rolls and resulting gameplay actors/state
Use stable spawn, location, quest-instance and reward-claim identities; a location is context and does not itself define personal, party or guild ownership
Validate eligibility, configured population limits and placement before spawning; failed spawn attempts must not count as successful spawns
Connect spawned objective actors to the correct quest instance so unrelated kills/interactions cannot advance another quest
Replicate spawned actors and quest offers/progress only to the intended recipients, including initialization for late joins
At the chosen roll event, retain the authoritative result for the quest/reward entitlement; repeated requests, UI reopening and failed grants must not reroll it
Preflight inventory capacity and grant item/currency rewards together; record claim completion only after successful delivery, with defined handling for XP and group rewards
Persist the quest instance, selected objectives/rewards and completed claims across supported save/load and reconnect flows
Keep population, spawn scheduling and quest-group selection within configurable server budgets, including level streaming and session lifecycle cleanup
acceptance_checks: Two connected players observe the intended shared spawns without each client generating duplicates
Spawn placement stays within the configured area and rejects blocked or otherwise invalid locations
Configured population limits and cooldowns survive repeated activation and actor destruction
Quest spawners choose only definitions eligible for the location and intended player/group
Quest-group selection follows recovered group semantics and dependencies
Repeated reward claims or full-inventory retries preserve the rolled result and cannot duplicate rewards
Late join, reconnect and save/load preserve the intended spawns, quest state and reward entitlements
